title: Classes: ListNode, TreeNode
short: Read and build the node classes LeetCode hands you.
what: A class is a blueprint for objects that bundle data with functions. __init__ runs when you create one and stores values on self. LeetCode gives you ListNode and TreeNode classes like this, and you add __lt__ when objects must go in a heap.
analogy: A form template. Each object is one filled-in copy: same boxes (val, next), different answers.

frames.label: head = ListNode(1)
frames.say: ListNode(1) builds an object and runs __init__. It stores self.val = 1 and self.next = None.

frames.label: head.next = ListNode(2)
frames.say: head.next = ListNode(2) links a second node. val and next are attributes: names stored on each object.
One more: ListNode(1, ListNode(2, ListNode(3))) builds the same chain in one line. It ends where next is None.

frames.label: while cur:
frames.say: cur = head, then while cur: ... cur = cur.next walks the chain. Each node only knows the next one.

frames.label: while cur:
frames.say: cur moves to 2, then 3, then None, which is false, so the loop ends. vals collected every value.

frames.label: def __lt__(self, other)
frames.say: __lt__ says what a < b means for two nodes. min(head.next, head) uses it and picks 1. sorted() and heapq use it too.

when: The problem gives you a ListNode or TreeNode
Build a small test list or tree yourself
Put custom objects in a heap
watch: Every method takes self first, and you store data with self.val = val, not val = val.
heapq compares items with <. Pushing nodes with no __lt__ raises TypeError on a tie, so push (val, i, node).
cur.next.val crashes when cur.next is None. Check it before you reach through.
